identity.title: Bladder volume estimate (transverse x sagittal, retention threshold)

technique.how: Curvilinear probe suprapubic, angled caudally. In transverse view measure maximal width and anteroposterior depth; rotate to sagittal and measure maximal height. Volume (mL) ~ width x depth x height x 0.52-0.75 (most devices use ~0.7). Alternatively use an automated bladder scanner. Repeat after voiding for post-void residual.
technique.prerequisites: Patient supine; know whether a catheter is present and functioning; operator trained in basic bladder POCUS or scanner use.

interpretation.positive_finding: A large bladder (commonly >300-400 mL post-void, or >500 mL in a patient unable to void) indicates urinary retention; in acute back pain it is a red flag for cauda equina syndrome.
interpretation.negative_finding: A small or empty bladder makes retention or bladder-outlet obstruction unlikely as the cause of AKI or discomfort, and reduces the likelihood of cauda equina syndrome (though red flags are more specific than sensitive).
interpretation.pitfalls: Ascites, ovarian cysts and pelvic collections can be mistaken for bladder; obesity, prior pelvic surgery, pregnancy and very small volumes reduce accuracy. Automated scanners overestimate with adjacent fluid and prolapse.
interpretation.changes_what: Retention volume: catheterise, measure residual, check renal function/POCUS kidneys; large PVR with back pain or neurological signs: emergent MRI for cauda equina.

estimates.population: 100 women at risk of postpartum urinary retention after vaginal delivery; automated bladder scanner vs catheterised volume
estimates.reference_standard: Urine volume obtained by urethral catheterisation
estimates.quote: The sensitivity and specificity for the scanner, using the clinically desired value of a 400-ml threshold, are 0.76 and 0.96,respectively.

sources.citation: Lukasse M, Cederkvist HR, Rosseland LA. Reliability of an automatic ultrasound system for detecting postpartum urinary retention after vaginal birth. Acta Obstet Gynecol Scand. 2007;86(10):1251-1255.

Theisen JG, Deveneau NE, Agrawal A, et al. The Accuracy of Portable Ultrasound Bladder Scanner Measurements of Postvoid Residual Volume in Women With Pelvic Organ Prolapse. Female Pelvic Med Reconstr Surg. 2020;26(2):141-145.

Dionne N, Adefolarin A, Kunzelman D, et al. What is the diagnostic accuracy of red flags related to cauda equina syndrome (CES), when compared to Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI)? A systematic review. Musculoskelet Sci Pract. 2019;42:125-133.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not rely on a scanner or single POCUS volume in patients with ascites, large pelvic masses, pregnancy or advanced prolapse; catheterise if in doubt.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Retention with back pain, saddle anaesthesia or leg weakness is cauda equina until proven otherwise: emergent MRI and spinal surgical referral; retention with AKI needs immediate decompression.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Automated scanners have low operator dependence; manual three-diameter POCUS varies with probe angle and chosen coefficient (0.52-0.75), so use one method consistently.
safety_scope.skill_assumption: Basic bladder POCUS (a few supervised scans) or trained use of an automated bladder scanner; estimates are from scanner devices, not manual formula.

extraction_notes: No meta-analysis of bladder POCUS volume accuracy for retention was found in budget. Lukasse 2007 (PubMed year field shows 2012 e-pub but journal issue 2007) gives sens/spec at the 400 mL threshold in postpartum women using an automated scanner; generalisability to elderly/AKI/post-operative patients is uncertain. Theisen 2020 entered as an agreement estimate (mean difference) with sens/spec null. Dionne 2019 pooled CES red-flag accuracy is reported in the abstract only as ranges across signs (sens 0.19-0.43, spec 0.62-0.88) without a urinary-retention-specific value, so cited without an estimate. Theisen 2020 agreement entry (mean difference 5.94 mL, 95% CI -3.8 to 15.7, Abstract) removed from estimates[] because it has no sens/spec/LR; it remains cited.
